# Real-corpus slice — provenance and expected result

Twelve instance files taken verbatim from the real corpus, not generated. This
exists so the scoring path can be exercised against genuine corpus data without
the 3 GB download, and so the parse/score/validate chain has a byte-exact
regression fixture.

## Source

`Techietal/Task-Scheduling-Dataset`, branch `main`, read through the GitHub API.
Every file below is reproduced byte-for-byte; the blob SHA is the proof.

Six cells: two families (GE, LA) x three processor counts (2, 4, 8) x two
instances. Deliberately small — this is a correctness fixture, not a benchmark
sample. Nothing here supports a performance claim.

## Format

D2: `n p`, then a preamble of `5*p` numbers, then the `n` by `p` computation
matrix, then the `n` by `n` communication matrix with `-1` for no edge. Token
count is exactly `2 + 5p + np + n^2` for every file, which is what distinguishes
D2 from D1 (`2 + 5p + np + n^2`) and D3 (`2 + p + np + n^2`) on these files.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py --data-root tests/fixtures/real-slice \
    --shard 0 --shards 1 --out /tmp/slice
python3 scripts/aggregate_benchmark.py --results /tmp/slice --out /tmp/slice/agg
```

Expected: 12 files scored, 0 failures, 0 invalid schedules.

## Expected result

`RESULTS/` holds the aggregate outputs from the run below: `summary.csv` and
`summary.json`. The per-instance `shard_00.jsonl` is not committed — it is
regenerated byte-for-byte by the reproduce command above, and it is the thing
being checked, so storing a copy would let a regression pass unnoticed.

Pooled geometric mean makespan over the 12 instances:

| Policy | Pooled | vs best | Strict wins | Shared wins |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ECTD | 267.26 | 0.00% | 1 | 6 |
| BPPTS | 283.19 | 5.96% | 1 | 1 |
| IPEFT | 284.31 | 6.38% | 0 | 3 |
| AEFT | 285.77 | 6.93% | 3 | 0 |
| LSTD | 288.24 | 7.85% | 0 | 2 |
| HEFT | 293.51 | 9.83% | 1 | 2 |

ECTD is best or joint-best on 7 of 12 instances and pooled-best. AEFT wins 3
strictly. On a 12-instance slice that ordering is not evidence of anything —
the standard error is enormous. It confirms the pipeline produces sane,
validated schedules on real data. The full 2,100-instance run is what would
support a claim.

## Note on duplicate placements

ECTD and LSTD each record 7 duplicate placements across the 12 instances; the
other four policies record none. That is expected: both duplicate the entry
task across processors, and `-1`-free entry rows in the LA instances give the
duplication logic something to place.
